modmenu.descriptionTranslation.cwb: Allows you to play Minecraft in a borderless fullscreen window.
neoforge.screen.mods.info.description.cw: Allows you to play Minecraft in a borderless fullscreen window.
cwb.options.fullscreenMode.tooltip:
§lExclusive§r fullscreen makes it cumbersome or outright impossible to use other apps while the game is running, yet it offers no performance benefits on this platform.

§lBorderless§r fullscreen aims to preserve the performance characteristics of exclusive fullscreen while incorporating common behaviors typically associated with windowed applications.

§lWindowed§r fullscreen preserves the characteristics of a windowed application while still delivering decent overall performance. Works best on systems with the dock and/or menu bar disabled or configured to hide automatically.
cwb.options.fullscreenMode.tooltip.macos:
§lExclusive§r fullscreen delivers great performance with minimal latency at the cost of usability, making it cumbersome or outright impossible to use other apps while the game is running.

§lBorderless§r fullscreen aims to preserve the characteristics of a windowed application at the cost of increased latency, while still delivering decent overall performance.

§lWindowed§r fullscreen retains the characteristics of borderless fullscreen while also keeping the menu bar visible at all times, which might prove useful for people who dislike the notch on newer MacBooks covering part of their game.
cwb.options.fullscreenMode.tooltip.windo:
§lExclusive§r fullscreen delivers great performance with minimal latency at the cost of usability, making it cumbersome or outright impossible to use other apps while the game is running.

§lBorderless§r fullscreen aims to preserve the performance characteristics of exclusive fullscreen while incorporating common behaviors typically associated with windowed applications.

§lWindowed§r fullscreen prioritizes the characteristics of a windowed application over performance. You will experience higher latency and may encounter significant performance degradation, depending on your system, hardware, and drivers.
cwb.options.exclusiveFullscreenType.tool: Controls which fullscreen mode is enabled when §oFullscreen§r is set to §oExclusive§r in §oVideo Settings§r.
cwb.options.borderlessFullscreenType.too: Controls which fullscreen mode is enabled when §oFullscreen§r is set to §oBorderless§r in §oVideo Settings§r.
cwb.options.windowedFullscreenType.toolt: Controls which fullscreen mode is enabled when §oFullscreen§r is set to §oWindowed§r in §oVideo Settings§r.
cwb.options.useDelayedFullscreen.tooltip:
Specifies whether to postpone entering fullscreen mode until Minecraft is fully loaded.

Enabling this option may result in a smoother startup sequence and can fix rare issues on systems with faulty drivers that do not immediately allow certain windows to enter fullscreen mode at a resolution that differs from the default one.
cwb.options.useScaledFramebuffer.tooltip:
Specifies whether to use a full-resolution framebuffer on platforms where screen coordinates can be scaled relative to pixel coordinates, such as §omacOS§r and §oWayland (Linux)§r.

Disabling this option may lead to a significant performance boost at the cost of image quality.
cwb.options.autoHideDock.tooltip: On supported platforms (e.g., §omacOS§r), specifies whether to automatically hide the dock in non-exclusive fullscreen modes, so it can be revealed by moving the mouse to the edge of the screen, instead of disabling it entirely.
cwb.options.autoHideMenuBar.tooltip: On supported platforms (e.g., §omacOS§r), specifies whether to automatically hide the menu bar in non-exclusive fullscreen modes, so it can be revealed by moving the mouse to the edge of the screen, instead of disabling it entirely.
cwb.options.pauseOnLostFocus.tooltip: Specifies whether the game should be automatically paused when its window loses focus.
cwb.options.pauseOnLostFocusDuringMultip: When §oPause on Lost Focus§r is enabled, specifies whether its effect should also apply to multiplayer sessions, where the game cannot be truly paused.
A windowed fullscreen mode that turns the game into a maximized borderless window.

Performance and UX characteristics of this mode may vary depending on the platform, but you can generally expect slightly higher latency than that of the default exclusive fullscreen mode due to the implicit V-Sync imposed on all windowed applications by most popular compositors.

Pairs best with systems with the dock and/or menu bar disabled or configured to hide automatically, or with players who prefer them to stay visible.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.minecraft:windowed.t:
A windowed fullscreen mode with performance and UX characteristics that vary depending on the platform.

On §lWindows§r, this mode is generally the best way to play the game, as it provides the benefits typical of a borderless fullscreen experience with zero to none performance and latency penalties; however, some users may experience annoying blinking each time the game window gains or loses focus.

On §lother platforms§r, this mode may cause significant performance degradation and/or usability issues, such as your system's dock remaining visible or even being rendered on top of the game.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.minecraft:default.to:
Minecraft's default exclusive fullscreen mode.

Provides great performance with minimal latency at the cost of usability - the game is automatically minimized each time its window loses focus.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.linux:borderless.too:
The default borderless fullscreen mode for Linux and other Unix-likes.

Provides great performance with minimal latency. Has no known downsides.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.macos:windowed.toolt:
The default windowed fullscreen mode for macOS.

Unlike §omacos:borderless§r, this mode leaves the menu bar visible at all times, which might prove useful for people who dislike the notch on newer MacBooks covering part of their game.

Provides decent performance, but has slightly higher latency than that of the exclusive fullscreen mode due to the implicit V-Sync imposed on all windowed applications by the OS.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.macos:borderless.too:
The default borderless fullscreen mode for macOS.

Provides decent performance, but has slightly higher latency than that of the default exclusive fullscreen mode due to the implicit V-Sync imposed on all windowed applications by the OS.
cwb.fullscreenTypes.windows:windowed.too:
The default windowed fullscreen mode for Windows.

Unlike §ominecraft:windowed§r, it does not suffer from the blinking issues, but it also lacks the performance benefits of the said mode.

Its latency is higher than that of the default exclusive fullscreen mode due to the implicit V-Sync imposed on all windowed applications by the OS. Additionally, some users may experience severe performance degradation, as Windows sometimes discards frames provided by windowed applications instead of rendering them, especially when performing background tasks it deems more important than that, such as downloading updates or indexing screenshots of your activity captured by Windows Recall.
